comparison.objective: Candidate calibrates and locks an articulated gripper stop; PR-1506 prepares a moka pot by controlling water level, inserting the coffee basket, and threading the upper chamber onto the base.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate needs two-tool coaxial countertorque and subsequent articulated verification; PR-1506 needs controlled pouring, basket placement, thread starting without cross-threading, and bimanual rotation of two vessel halves.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires a released 90° opening retained through three cycles with ≤2° drift and both nuts retained; PR-1506 requires 122.5–155.8 mL water, basket/coffee present, straight gasket-compressing thread engagement, limited spill, upright release, and no cross-threading.
comparison.reason: Although both include bimanual rotation and tightening, PR-1506 tests fluid dosing and mating two large threaded bodies, not counterholding a precision adjuster during jam-nut locking or verifying a retained motion stop. Numeric outcome and damage conditions are present across its versions.
